title: Dice Roller
story: Dungeons & Dragons runs on dice: d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20. 'Roll 3d6 for your strength score.' 'Roll a d20 to hit the dragon.' Build a dice roller that handles any number of any-sided dice — the essential tool for every tabletop gamer.
why: Dice rolling teaches random number generation in a range, summing multiple rolls, and configurable parameters — a practical simulation program.
analogy: A fistful of dice shaken in a cup and spilled onto the table. Each die is independent, each face equally likely. Your dice roller is the digital cup — specify how many dice to shake and how many sides each has, and it spills them all at once, computing the total.
try_it: Simulate 1000 rolls of 3d6 and track the frequency of each possible sum (3-18). Which sum is most common? Why? Add 'advantage' (roll 2d20, take highest) and 'disadvantage' (take lowest). Roll a full D&D character: six stats using 4d6-drop-lowest.
tips: Rolling multiple dice creates a bell curve — sums near the middle are more likely
common_mistakes: Forgetting the `+ 1` — without it, results are 0..sides-1
Using the same seed for every die — leads to identical rolls
Taking average of dice instead of sum — different distributions
